newsitem.title: UK: Closing overseas stock market indices.
newsitem.headline: Closing overseas stock market indices.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading stock index powered to its second highest close in a broad-based rally that continued to feed off a favourable outlook for British interest rates and the pound. The FTSE 100 closed at 5,075.8, up 43.9 points, or 0.87 percent.

FRANKFURT - German stocks posted gains on modest volumes, heartened by an upbeat close on Wall Street overnight, the stable dollar and the Bundesbank's decision not to raise a key interest rate. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,363.09, up 29.96 points, or 0.69 percent. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,377.51, up 44.36 points, or 1.02 percent.
PARIS - French stocks closed up half a percentage point, supported by dollar firmness, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,998.57, up 15.13 points, or 0.51 percent.
ZURICH - Insecurity about further developments in U.S. and German interest rates led Swiss stocks to a lower close. The Swiss market index closed at 5,808.4, down 17.2 points, or 0.30 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks recovered modestly from the previous day's nearly 4 percent plunge in the benchmark index, as stability in the dollar and U.S. stocks prompted investors to hunt for bargains in blue-chip exporter issues that had been hit hard Monday, brokers said. The 225-stock Nikkei average closed at 19.099.11, up 274.93 points, or 1.46 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended weak, reversing gains made earlier in the day, as a rising U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield and an increase in mortgage lending rates by two major banks prompted a slide in property stocks. The Hang Seng index closed at 16,383.41, down 77.06 points, or 0.47 percent.

SYDNEY - The Australian stock market fell away at the close to end the day near its lows after opening firmer in line with a stronger Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,650.5, down 16.7 points, or 0.63 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks finished off highs, failing to react positively to a better June producer price inflation and dragged lower by De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.'s results, which dealers described as "disappointing." The All-Stock index closed at 7,579.9, down 3.2 points, or 0.04 percent. The All-Gold index closed at 1,017.1, up 0.8 points, or 0.08 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9,267.7, up 28.3 points, or 0.31 percent.
